scope: chipped, loose, displaced, or knocked-out tooth or minor mouth injury after a household or sports accident; must confirm baby vs permanent tooth before reinsertion advice
patterns: my child knocked out a tooth
my baby tooth was knocked out
my tooth is loose after being hit
child hit mouth on a table
can I put a knocked-out tooth back in
tooth moved after a sports accident
response: For a knocked-out permanent tooth, act quickly. Handle the tooth by the crown, not the root. If it is clearly a permanent tooth and you are comfortable, gently rinse it with milk or saline and try to place it back in the socket, or keep it in milk or a recommended storage solution while going straight to urgent dental care. Do not reinsert a baby tooth. For a chip or loose tooth, avoid chewing on that side and arrange urgent dental advice.
red_flags: loss of consciousness or head-injury symptoms
tooth appears to have gone into the airway
